correctness.rationale: PASS: Johnson geodesic intervals are precisely constant-rank Boolean intervals [intersection,union]_k by the shortest-path exchange argument. A support is shattered iff each member has a coordinate privately present or privately absent. For t>=3, distinct witness columns give t<=max{n-k+1,k+1,n-2}, with matching mixed constructions P,Q,R and pure extremal cases. Equality at t=n-2 forces a unique partition because column multiplicities 1,q,t-1 differ (p,q>=2); separate k=3, n-k=3 and (4,2) exceptions are counted. Independent enumeration confirmed 20 rank/n cases up to n=7 and complete small graph convex families, with no extrapolation from these tests to the universal theorem.
